noAccess.title: You cannot open Quality rules
noAccess.body: It needs the permission quality.rules.view. An administrator gives it in Admin › Roles & permissions (the quality inspector, production manager and floor supervisor roles hold it).

head.intro: Who may sign what, who is told of what and how fast, and how results are counted. A looser rule asks for a fresh code; a stricter one never does.

scope.label: Whose rules
scope.companyHint: This company follows the rules of every company wherever it keeps nothing of its own; what it keeps here is added to them.
scope.allHint: These rules apply to every company that keeps nothing of its own. Changing them needs a role over every company.

live.changedBody: Read them again before you save: your unsaved changes are dropped.

stepUp.title: Confirm with your code
stepUp.loosen: A looser rule of who may sign what takes effect once you confirm it with a fresh code from your authenticator.

card.failed: These rules could not be read
card.neverChanged: Never changed here: the rules above are the defaults and what is inherited.

held.noRight: Changing these rules needs quality.settings.manage for this company.
held.noRightAll: Changing the rules of every company needs quality.settings.manage over every company.
held.offline: No connection: changes wait until the page is back online.
held.busy: Wait: the last change is still being saved.
held.reading: Wait: the page is still reading.
held.allOn: Every ticked rule is on already.
held.allOff: Every ticked rule is off already.
held.starterAll: The suggested rules are rules of every company: they need quality.alerts.manage over every company.

duties.title: Separation of duties and four-eyes

release.question: Who releases finished garments?
release.alone: The inspector who signed may release alone
release.aloneHint: When they made none of the garments. A second person only when a condition below asks it.
release.always: Every release needs a second person
release.alwaysHint: After the inspector's signature, someone else always releases.
release.default: Nothing set: the inspector who made none of the garments releases alone (the default).

rule.ALWAYS: Every release needs a second person

conditions.question: A second person is also needed for
conditions.oneRecord: An overridden result and a conditional release are one record (a pass over a computed fail): one tick covers both.

condition.CUSTOMER: The garments of the customers listed here

duties.conditionFromAll: The rules of every company ask this: change it under Every company.
duties.coveredByAlways: Every release needs a second person already.

hold.question: Who releases a hold?
hold.someoneElse: Someone other than the person who placed it
hold.someoneElseHint: The person who placed a hold never releases it.
hold.placer: The person who placed it may release it too
hold.placerHint: For a factory with one quality person on a shift.
hold.followPlacer: Now: the person who placed it may release it

duties.loosens_one: This change loosens {count} rule: it asks for the reason and a fresh code
duties.loosens_other: This change loosens {count} rules: it asks for the reason and a fresh code

loosen.title: Confirm a looser rule
loosen.reasonHint: Kept with the change in the audit trail.
loosen.codeHint: Apply asks for a fresh code from your authenticator.
loosen.reasonHeld: Say why first, in at least 3 characters.

code.RELEASE_ALONE: From now on an inspector who made none of the garments releases alone.
code.OVERRIDE_ALONE: From now on one person can release overridden results and conditional releases.
code.CUSTOMER_ALONE: From now on the listed customers' garments no longer need a second person.
code.CUSTOMERS_REMOVED: From now on the garments of {count} customer(s) taken off the list no longer need a second person.
code.PLACER_RELEASES: From now on the person who placed a hold may release it too.

results.title: Result rules
results.description: How results are computed and counted.

stop.question: When a sample already rejects the lot
stop.finishHint: Every unit of the sample is inspected, also after a class rejects the lot.
stop.stopHint: Once a class reaches its reject number, the inspection may be signed failed.
stop.followStop: Now: stop at the reject number
stop.planWins: An inspection plan version that says otherwise wins.

undo.label: Undo window after a bench scan
undo.hint: From {min} to {max} seconds; 0: a bench scan is never undone.

results.undoRange: The undo window is a whole number of seconds from 0 to 300.

signers.title: Who signs, always
signers.description: The rules that are not settings, with their why.

monitoring.title: Who floor records name (the maker check)
monitoring.WORKER: Scans record the worker: the maker check reads the scans
monitoring.STATION: Station only: the maker check is a signed statement

separations.title: Separations every role keeps
separations.broken: A custom role does not keep it: {roles}. Change the role in Admin › Roles & permissions.
separations.how: The system roles keep every separation (a test holds them to it); one record's own checks refuse a person who made the goods, wrote the plan or placed the hold.

alerts.title: Alerts and escalation
alerts.description: Who gets what and how fast.
alerts.failed: The alert rules could not be read
alerts.capaNote: Corrective actions: the escalation is a task in the people's own tasks.
alerts.shadowed: Not for this company: it keeps its own rules of this event.
alerts.howTold: A rule rings the bell of the people it names who may see the record; e-mail reaches them only through their daily digest, when they keep it on. Nothing reaches a customer or a supplier.

empty.title: No alert rule yet
empty.body_one: Start from the suggested rule, or add your own.
empty.body_other: Start from the {count} suggested rules, or add your own.

event.RELEASE_WAITING_SECOND_PERSON: Release waiting for the second person

row.testHint: Rings your bell once with this rule's words.

ruleDialog.fixed: Fixed once the rule is added.
ruleDialog.both: The owner and everyone with a role
ruleDialog.nobodyNamed: A certificate names nobody: the rule tells a role.
ruleDialog.days: Days before the last valid day
ruleDialog.daysHint: Up to 6 numbers from 1 to 730, e.g. 180, 90, 30. Once each, only the latest one reached.
ruleDialog.waitHint: Told once, when the record has waited this long.
ruleDialog.waitEventHint: 0: at once. More: once, if it is still so after this long.
ruleDialog.emailHow: E-mail reaches a person through their daily digest of the bell, when they keep it on.
ruleDialog.capaHow: A corrective action escalates as a task to these people (the corrective action keeps its reminders).

problem.audience: A certificate names nobody: tell a role.
problem.wait: A whole number, at most 30 days.
problem.days: Give 1 to 6 different numbers of days from 1 to 730.
problem.companyId: Pick a company you keep rules for.

remove.body_one: Nobody is told by it any more. The audit trail keeps what it was.
remove.body_other: Nobody is told by them any more. The audit trail keeps what they were.

problem.stale: Someone changed this meanwhile: it was read again; make your change again.
problem.conflict: This clashes with what is stored: read the page again.
problem.reason: Say why, in at least 3 characters.
problem.changedMeanwhile: The rules in force changed meanwhile: read them again, then loosen them with the reason and a fresh code.
problem.customers: Only customers are listed, each once.
problem.invalid: The change was refused as it is.
problem.stepUp: The looser rule needs a fresh code.
problem.gone: This rule is no longer there.
problem.signedOut: You are signed out: sign in again.
problem.offline: No answer from the server: we do not know whether it was saved. Try again.
problem.read: The server did not answer as expected.
problem.ruleGone: The rule the address names is no longer there.

done.duties: Who may sign what is saved.
done.dutiesLoosened: The looser rule is saved, with your reason.
done.tested: A test is on its way to your bell.
